title: An onion price gap without cost evidence
summary: Lasalgaon → Azadpur, January 2014: a ₹164 per quintal median price gap on 24 matched days. No cited cost evidence for this period.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2014: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 24 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).

OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: January 2014
scenes.caption: Lasalgaon (Nashik) is India's best-known onion auction; Azadpur (Delhi) is the largest terminal market it feeds, a link the RBI paper describes.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 24 matched days, Lasalgaon reported a median ₹945 per quintal; Azadpur reported ₹1,126 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹164/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹164 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,115 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,115 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~13 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: The reported gap was ₹164 per quintal, but we have no cited cost evidence for January 2014, so no after-cost result is claimed.

conclusion: The reported gap was ₹164 per quintal, but we have no cited cost evidence for January 2014, so no after-cost result is claimed.
